name: Rohan Shah
current_role: Co-founder and Chief Revenue Officer, Extend (product protection / extended warranty platform, San Francisco)
profile: Stanford 2014 graduate who co-founded Extend in 2019 with Woody Levin and others; the company lets merchants offer extended warranties and protection plans and handles claims, with customers such as Peloton, iRobot and Logitech. He is listed as Founder & CRO / head of partnerships. Not to be confused with Extend (paywithextend, virtual cards, CEO Andrew Jamison).
interesting_fact: Named to Forbes 30 Under 30 in 2020 for co-founding Extend, which grew to 100+ full-time employees in under two years.
deep_cut_fact: His first startup after Stanford, which sold to startups, didn't work out; he then became a product lead in BCG's Digital Ventures group to build skills before co-founding Extend. His parents are both entrepreneurs who started a company together in 1987. Quote: 'I was always the best at learning by doing.'
notes: Hurun's 'Extend' here is the warranty company (extend.com), not the fintech paywithextend.com. NYSE TV lists him as 'Extend Founder & CRO' (https://tv.nyse.com/ceos-leaders/videos/extend-founder-cro-rohan-shah). No published personal contact found.

name: Jerome Ternynck
current_role: Founder of SmartRecruiters (acquired by SAP, closed Sept 2025); MarketScreener lists him as Chairman since April 2023; Rebecca Carr is now SmartRecruiters CEO
profile: French entrepreneur who spent a decade in recruiting software, founding Lumesse (formerly in the UK) in 1999 and serving as CEO until 2010. He moved from Paris to San Francisco in 2010 and founded SmartRecruiters, a talent-acquisition SaaS used by 4,000+ organisations, which SAP agreed to acquire in August 2025.
interesting_fact: SAP announced the acquisition of SmartRecruiters on Aug 1, 2025 and completed it on Sept 11, 2025, planning to integrate it with SuccessFactors while keeping it available standalone.
deep_cut_fact: After moving from Paris to San Francisco in 2010 he raised $1M in seed money; SmartRecruiters launched in summer 2011 as a free job-posting app and didn't launch its first paid product until May 2014. His stated goal: 'I wanted to make hiring a quality business, and I wanted to give people a job they loved.'
notes: Post-acquisition role unclear; best route likely via SmartRecruiters/SAP press or LinkedIn. Past interview: French Tech San Francisco podcast (https://podcasts.apple.com/fr/podcast/itw-j%C3%A9r%C3%B4me-ternynck-ceo-founder-smartrecruiters/id1622892563).

name: Matan Bar
current_role: Co-founder and CEO of Melio; leads the combined Xero/Melio US business after Xero's acquisition (completed Oct 2025)
profile: Haifa-born Israeli founder who studied computer science at Tel Aviv University, co-founded The Gifts Project (sold to eBay), then spent six years at PayPal leading global consumer P2P payments. He co-founded Melio, a US SMB bill-pay platform, with Ilan Atias and Ziv Paz; Xero bought it for $2.5B upfront in 2025, its largest-ever deal.
interesting_fact: Xero agreed to buy Melio for US$2.5B upfront in June 2025 (up to ~$3B with earn-outs); Bar was slated to lead the combined US business reporting to Xero CEO Sukhinder Singh Cassidy.
deep_cut_fact: Melio's original idea was called 'Payper' (pay per check) - the team would mail paper checks for businesses. His first startup, The Gifts Project, was started in his last university semester at 24 with Ron Gura and sold to eBay when he was 26.
notes: Has appeared on many podcasts (Aleph 'Invested', Fintech Leaders, Founder Real Talk) - podcast-friendly.

name: Tomas Cupr
current_role: Founder and CEO, Rohlik Group; also heads AI-agent startup Duvo AI (founded 2025)
profile: Czech serial entrepreneur (Tomáš Čupr) who founded deals site Slevomat and food-delivery app Dáme jídlo (later sold to Delivery Hero) before launching online grocer Rohlik in 2014, now a pan-European group (Knuspr, Gurkerl, Kifli, Sezamo). He also founded the investment firm TCF Capital and in 2026 Duvo AI raised a $32M Series A led by Balderton.
interesting_fact: His AI startup Duvo AI, founded in 2025, builds agents that learn company workflows and automate them inside existing systems like SAP; clients include Morrisons and Allegro, and in Oct 2026 it was raising $32M led by Balderton Capital.
deep_cut_fact: A Brno University of Technology IT student, he ended up in Sheffield, England in summer 2004 with three friends, lived there about five years doing web development, internet marketing and car financing, and started building Slevomat from Sheffield. He says 'Great service wins' is a lesson he learned in Britain.
notes: Frequent guest in Czech media/podcasts (CzechCrunch, Forbes CZ). Aspen Institute CE profile exists.

name: Criag Iley
current_role: Founder of Business Finance Market (UK SME lending platform), per 2022 interview; current role not verified
profile: UK banker (name is Craig Iley; input has a typo) who joined Atom Bank from Santander as commercial/business banking director and is described as a co-founder of Atom Bank and of Bank North. He later founded Business Finance Market, a platform matching lenders with SMEs. Atom's commonly cited founders are Anthony Thomson and Mark Mullen, so 'founder' attribution is loose.
interesting_fact: He argues the UK has room for about ten more SME lenders in a ~£200bn market, and that a new bank needs 6-10 years to build a £5bn lending book; he points to Germany's tiered banking system as a model.
notes: Hurun listing 'Atom Bank founder' is a stretch; he was an early senior exec (Finextra: 'Atom names Santander's Craig Iley as commercial director', https://www.finextra.com/pressarticle/55176/atom-names-santanders-craig-iley-as-commercial-director). Low profile; likely not UHNW. Alive status not specifically confirmed.

name: Timo Boldt
current_role: Founder and CEO of Gousto (announced Sept 2026 he will step down to become a board director once a successor is appointed, expected H1 2027)
profile: German-born former banker and Cambridge Judge EMBA (2014) alumnus who founded UK meal-kit company Gousto in 2012, initially packing and delivering kits himself. Gousto became a unicorn in 2022, delivers 80M+ meals a year and posted 2025 revenue of £342m with record £45m adjusted EBITDA. He also founded Bento (2021) to license Gousto's tech.
interesting_fact: Named EY World Entrepreneur Of The Year Class of 2023 (UK); about 95% of Gousto staff are shareholders.
deep_cut_fact: Long banking hours and takeaway dinners inspired Gousto; at 26 he quit, moved into university housing to fund it, packed every meal by hand, delivered them himself and took no salary for three years. His advice: 'You will be rejected a thousand times...'
notes: Leadership transition news: https://www.grocerygazette.co.uk/2026/09/17/gousto-founder-step-down/ . Frequent conference speaker (London Tech Week, Sifted Summit).

name: Philipp Nieland
current_role: Co-founder of PPRO (cross-border payments infrastructure, London/Munich); current role not verified
profile: German co-founder of PPRO, which provides local/alternative payment-method acquiring and processing to PSPs such as PayPal and Stripe. Crunchbase says he studied economics and computer science and founded PPRO in 2006; MarketScreener credits Nieland and Tobias Schreyer as founders. PPRO's backers include PayPal, Citi Ventures and HPE Growth.
interesting_fact: PPRO raised a $50M round led by PayPal, with Citi Ventures participating and HPE Growth reinvesting.
notes: Very low public profile; founder attribution rests on Crunchbase (https://crunchbase.com/person/philipp-nieland) and MarketScreener. Not to be confused with co-founder Philipp Bock. No published press email found on ppro.com.

name: Zheng Kai
current_role: Listed as co-founder and Chief Strategy Officer of XTransfer (single aggregator source; unverified)
profile: One of six co-founders of XTransfer, a Shanghai-based B2B cross-border payments platform for SME exporters founded in 2017 by Bill (Guobiao) Deng with former Ant Group colleagues. Only one aggregator profile names 'Kai Zheng (Co-founder and CSO)'; no official XTransfer source found confirming his role.
interesting_fact: XTransfer was founded in 2017 by Bill Deng and five other co-founders, largely former Ant Group employees, to serve Chinese small exporters.
notes: Identity weakly sourced (https://yespress.io/xtransfer.md). The public face of XTransfer is founder/CEO Bill Deng; route via company.

name: Sherwin Gandhi
current_role: Co-founder and director of Jeeves (cross-border corporate cards and spend management for Latin America and beyond); also an angel investor
profile: Co-founder of Jeeves, a fintech offering multi-currency corporate cards, payments and expense management to startups in Latin America, Canada and Europe, led by CEO Dileep Thazhmon. Aggregator profiles list Gandhi as founder, executive officer and director, with an RPI undergraduate degree and around eight angel investments.
notes: Very thin public footprint; role sourced only from aggregators (https://www.pipeseed.com/investor/sherwin-gandhi-936507, https://seedtable.com/person/Sherwin_Gandhi-39W6XNJ, https://ch.marketscreener.com/insider/SHERWIN-GANDHI-A39CHL/erfahrung). Public face of Jeeves is CEO Dileep Thazhmon. No published press email found on tryjeeves.com.

name: Tanay Tandon
current_role: CEO, Commure (healthcare technology; merged with Athelas in Oct 2023)
profile: Silicon Valley founder with a machine-learning background who co-founded Athelas with Deepika Bodapati (YC S16), starting with an in-home blood-testing device and expanding into remote patient monitoring and revenue-cycle software. After Athelas merged with Commure in October 2023 he became CEO of the combined company, with Bodapati as COO; Commure now focuses on AI tools for health systems.
interesting_fact: During Athelas's first clinical trial in 2016 at a hospital in Juárez, Mexico, Tandon spotted a white blood cell count above 40,000 with immature cells - the patient was later confirmed to have leukemia.
deep_cut_fact: He and co-founder Deepika Bodapati met on the high-school science-fair circuit, first bonding on a flight to a competition; Athelas's first Mountain View office was 'a barely refurbished liquor store.'
notes: Speaks publicly (e.g. Slush 2024 with Initialized: https://blog.initialized.com/2024/11/supercharging-healthcare-with-tanay-tandon-at-slush-2024/). Hurun lists Athelas; the company now operates as Commure. No published press email found on commure.com.

name: Kisik Bae
current_role: Founder and CEO, RIDI Corporation (Seoul; e-books, webtoons and web novels)
profile: Bae Ki-sik, a Seoul National University electrical engineering graduate and former Samsung Electronics corporate-venture investor, founded RIDI in 2008 betting on smartphone-era content. RIDI became Korea's leading e-book platform and then shifted toward webtoons and web novels; it raised KRW 120B from GIC and others in 2022 at unicorn valuation.
interesting_fact: RIDI first tried producing comics with dozens of hired artists, then pivoted to e-books because text only needed digitizing; despite skeptical publishers, he had deals with about 200 publishers by 2011.
deep_cut_fact: Before founding RIDI he worked on Samsung Electronics' corporate venture investment team; in the early days, he says, 'I would visit publishers during the day and develop the service at night with our developers.'
notes: RIDI was selected for the Tokyo Stock Exchange Asia Startup Hub in 2024 and 2025 (https://www.asiae.co.kr/en/article/2025092908590212822). No published press email found.

name: Lutz Gerlach
current_role: Co-founder and COO, Staffbase (employee communications platform, Chemnitz, Germany)
profile: German former academic (doctorate in business/managerial economics, senior researcher at Chemnitz University of Technology) who co-founded productivity app Hojoki in 2011 and then Staffbase in 2014 with Martin Böhringer and Frank Wolf. Staffbase grew into a leading employee-app and intranet platform, reaching unicorn valuation with Series D (2021) and E (2022) rounds.
interesting_fact: Staffbase is headquartered in Chemnitz, eastern Germany, a rare unicorn outside Berlin/Munich, and grew out of the same founding team as the earlier Hojoki startup.
deep_cut_fact: Before Staffbase he was a senior researcher at Chemnitz University of Technology (doctorate in business/managerial economics), then co-founded and served as COO of productivity-app startup Hojoki, founded in Chemnitz in March 2011.
notes: Role sourced from Staffbase recruiting pages and MarketScreener; CEO Martin Böhringer is the more public face.

name: Jose Vargas
current_role: Co-founder and President, HealthCare.com (Miami/New York insurtech)
profile: Miami-based serial internet entrepreneur who has built online companies in Miami for about two decades and co-founded investment firm PeopleFund. In 2014 he co-founded HealthCare.com with Howard Yeh and Jeff Smedsrud - a marketplace to compare and enroll in health insurance and Medicare plans plus its own Pivot Health products. It reached a $1B+ valuation with a $180M Oaktree-led round in 2021.
interesting_fact: HealthCare.com's $180M round (led by Oaktree) made it one of Miami's unicorns; staff grew from ~100 to 425 in a year, and its CEO quipped 'it doesn't hurt that we have the world's greatest url.'
deep_cut_fact: He co-founded PeopleFund, which backed HealthCare.com, and earlier founded, grew and sold other online platform businesses; on the #MiamiTech Pod (Ep 53, Feb 2022) he discussed two decades of building online companies and M&A in Miami.
notes: Not to be confused with journalist Jose Antonio Vargas. No published press email found on healthcare.com.

name: Mark Frank
current_role: Co-founder and CEO, SonderMind (Denver behavioral-health platform)
profile: West Point graduate and former Army officer, Kellogg MMM ('07) and ex-Morgan Stanley investment banker turned serial healthcare entrepreneur. He co-founded SonderMind in 2014 with clinician Sean Boyd to make in-network therapy accessible, partly after struggling to find a therapist that fit his needs and insurance; it raised a $150M Series C in 2021.
interesting_fact: As an Army officer he led three platoons between ages 22 and 24 before serving as a company executive officer.
deep_cut_fact: In 2009 he founded Denver Cyberknife (later Anova Cancer Care), personally guaranteeing over $6M of bank debt - 'the alternative to success was personal insolvency' - and sold it, returning 12x to his outside investor.
notes: Frequent podcast guest (HLTH 'The Beat', others); veteran-focused - featured by NVCA: https://nvca.org/startup-story/the-denver-unicorn-making-in-network-mental-healthcare-actually-work-for-patients-therapists-and-veterans/ Writes contributed columns for MedCity News (https://medcitynews.com/author/mfrank). No published press email found on sondermind.com.

name: Brian Beard
current_role: Co-founder and Chief Legal Officer (also styled Chief Global Strategy & Legal Officer), Colossal Biosciences
profile: Veteran Austin technology lawyer with 35+ years of practice, including 15 years as managing partner at Wilson Sonsini Goodrich & Rosati and a stint at Gunderson Dettmer. He joined de-extinction startup Colossal Biosciences (founded 2021 by Ben Lamm and George Church) at its $15M seed launch and leads strategy, partnerships and licensing.
interesting_fact: Colossal, which aims to revive the woolly mammoth and other extinct species, hired him as one of a half-dozen senior executives when it announced its $15M seed round in 2021.
deep_cut_fact: Over his career he has closed thousands of technology transactions and hundreds of public offerings for companies and underwriters.
notes: Behind-the-scenes legal/strategy role; Colossal's public face is CEO Ben Lamm.

name: Tang Dingguo
current_role: Listed as board director and chair of the scientific advisory committee of StemiRna Therapeutics (Shanghai mRNA company)
profile: StemiRna Therapeutics (斯微生物), a Shanghai mRNA vaccine/therapeutics developer founded in 2016 by CEO Li Hangwen with scientists who returned from MD Anderson, lists 唐定国 (Tang Dingguo) as director and SAB chair; a shareholder 'TANG DEAN G' holds ~5.95%. This may be cancer-stem-cell scientist Dean G. Tang (Roswell Park; 16 years at MD Anderson), but that link is not confirmed by a source.
notes: Founder attribution by Hurun is doubtful: 36Kr lists Li Hangwen as founder/CEO with 71.45% (https://pitchhub.36kr.com/project/1678467395941379). Possible match Dean Tang, PhD (https://www.roswellpark.org/dean-tang) - verify before outreach.

name: Huang Musen
profile: Listed by Hurun as founder of 'Zhongxin Breeding' (agriculture, valued ~$1B). English and Chinese searches (黄木森, 中新育种, 种业) found no source confirming the person, the company's Chinese name or his role.
notes: Could not identify. Need the company's registered Chinese name (e.g. from the Hurun Global Unicorn Index Chinese edition or a corporate registry) to research further.

name: Justas Dauparas
current_role: Protein-design scientist; Hurun lists him as a Xaira Therapeutics founder, but no Xaira source confirms his current role
profile: Machine-learning protein-design researcher, formerly a project scientist in David Baker's lab at the UW Institute for Protein Design, who led ProteinMPNN (Science 2022) and LigandMPNN (Nature Methods 2025). Xaira, launched in 2024 with $1B+ under CEO Marc Tessier-Lavigne, was founded to build on IPD models including RFdiffusion and ProteinMPNN.
interesting_fact: ProteinMPNN, the sequence-design model he led at the Baker lab, runs in about one second - over 200x faster than the previous best software - and its designs were more likely to fold as intended in lab tests.
deep_cut_fact: On building ProteinMPNN he said: 'Neural networks are easy to train if you have a ton of data... We had to go in and identify which features in these molecules are the most important.'
notes: GeekWire (2024) describes him as one of the scientists behind ProteinMPNN in its Xaira coverage (https://www.geekwire.com/2024/inside-the-seattle-labs-of-xaira-the-ai-powered-startup-launched-with-1b-from-investors/); I couldn't open the article to confirm his Xaira title. An academic, not a typical founder-CEO; route via Xaira.

name: Avi Turgeman
current_role: Co-founder and CEO, IronVest (New York / Herzliya; personal online security and biometric fraud prevention)
profile: Israeli Unit 8200 veteran who founded behavioral-biometrics company BioCatch (with Benny Rosenbaum, c. 2011) and served as its CTO; BioCatch later took a $145M investment from Bain Capital. He was on the founding team of Tapingo (acquired by Grubhub in 2018) and in 2022 launched IronVest with a $23M seed round led by Accomplice.
interesting_fact: BioCatch is built on his theory, first pursued while serving in military intelligence, that people interact with machines in unique, measurable ways - the basis of behavioral biometrics for fraud detection.
deep_cut_fact: He met IronVest co-founder and CTO Kfir Yeshayahu while both served in the 8200 unit, and he was a founding team member of campus food-ordering app Tapingo alongside IronVest co-founders Guy Bauman and Yaron Dror.
notes: No published press email found on ironvest.com. Also listed as co-founder of VocalZoom (theorg).

name: Drew Patel
current_role: Co-founder, Andalusia Labs (creator of Karak Network restaking/shared-security platform and Risk Harbor)
profile: University of Missouri computer-science graduate and young serial founder who left a 2021 Coinbase software-engineering internship to start Andalusia Labs with Raouf Ben-Har, whom he met at Coinbase. Andalusia built Risk Harbor and the Karak shared-security network and raised ~$48-50M at a unicorn valuation from investors including Lightspeed, Mubadala, Coinbase and Bain Capital Crypto.
interesting_fact: He met co-founder Raouf Ben-Har while both were at Coinbase in 2021 and left his internship there to found Andalusia Labs.
deep_cut_fact: His first startup (c. 2017) was Bloodchain, a blockchain blood-tracking system for developing nations, where he was CTO; he says he chose entrepreneurship over a BCG internship after high school and sums up his advice as 'go, work, and inquire.'
notes: Main source is IQ.wiki (crypto wiki, community-edited); treat details as moderately reliable. No published press email found.
